source.title: SpIn-ViT: Designing a Sparsity-Induced Vision Transformer That Is Mechanistically Interpretable

record.file_problem: Whole paper text, including appendix, is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates neuron-derived features in vision transformers using human and automated interpretability measures, extending neuron interpretability work to a new modality. It does not measure the proportion of neurons with one main job, as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates interpretability of SAE neuron activations and their highlighted image regions, but does not audit neuron poles, count interpretable neurons, test explanations on held-out activations, or assess the specified language-model and InceptionV1 claims. Its AI and human ratings and insertion/deletion results are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not measure the specific outcomes named in the versions. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study builds and trains SAE latents in a ViT to be interpretable, then compares its method with baselines on accuracy, mask agreement, human ratings and insertion/deletion. It never counts the share of a model's native neurons with one job. It does not test explanations against held-out activations or touch language models, InceptionV1 or attribution graphs. Its SAE features are trained for interpretability, which induces the property rather than measuring it arising. It mentions polysemanticity only as motivation and neither tests nor uses the claim. The reader's 'tests/T3' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that jointly training a ViT with a TopK SAE, plus center and orthogonality losses, yields more interpretable patch-level latents than post-hoc SAEs while keeping accuracy: 88.30% average, 8.84 points over PatchSAE, about 4x the AI score and over 2x the human score. The latents also give neurosymbolic rule sets with 5.97% higher accuracy and 58.85% fewer rules.
record.recipe_differences: This paper jointly trains a vision transformer and modified SAE for image classification; it does not perform the language-model neuron-pole audit or held-out explanation evaluation described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability scores differ by method variant and dataset; the paper reports higher scores for SpIn-ViT (Ours) than the comparison methods across all nine datasets in the AI evaluation, and higher human ratings on both rated datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly trained TopK-SAE latents (SpIn-ViT Ours) agree more with SAM3 concept masks than PatchSAE and ablation variants on all nine datasets (avg 3.08 vs PatchSAE 1.27 on a 1–5 scale).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training SAE latents jointly with the classification objective yields ViT patch features whose highlighted regions agree more with concept masks than post-hoc SAE features.

fits_no_version.finding: Twelve raters scored the most active SAE neuron's highlighted region per image, 100 images from Flowers102 and FGVC. SpIn-ViT Ours averaged 4.10 against PatchSAE 1.85.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Human-rated coherence of the top SAE neuron's highlighted region is higher for jointly trained SAE latents than for post-hoc SAE latents in ViTs.

fits_no_version.finding: Insertion AUC 0.830 (highest) and deletion AUC 0.142 (lowest) for SpIn-ViT Ours, averaged over datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jointly trained SAE neuron activations rank image patches more faithfully to the model's predictions.

record.problems: The human evaluation covers 100 images from two datasets and 12 participants; the AI score is a normalized agreement with SAM3-generated masks and is not a direct measure of neuron-level semantic exclusivity or the proportion of interpretable neurons. The reported insertion/deletion metrics do not establish one-job-per-neuron.
record.rows_left_out: The aggregate means in Tables 2 and 3 were omitted because the per-dataset table results are recorded. Per-dataset insertion/deletion figure curves and their qualitative descriptions in Figures 4 and 5 and Appendix A.2 were omitted; the two explicit aggregate AUC results are included.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or one-job, two-job and unexplained shares.
No language models, dense/MoE comparison or scale series; no share of interpretable neurons in any model.
No InceptionV1 or cat-and-car neuron analysis; no recursive generalization vs superposition test.

No share of interpretable native neurons across architectures or tools. Comparisons are between SAE training variants built for interpretability, scored by mask mIoU and ratings, not interpretable-neuron fractions.
No attribution graphs, no replacement model, no reconstruction-error comparison.
No check of activating-example explanations against firing on held-out inputs.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

record.verdict_notes: All rows compare the study's own method with baselines, and the units are SAE latents trained for interpretability, not native model neurons. They are correctly linked to 'none' and kept only as fits_no_version context. The AI and human ratings score one top neuron per image, not the fraction of neurons with a coherent job. Nothing bears on V1–V7, so no verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or neuron-pole counts; no one-job, two-related-jobs, or not-understood proportions.
No cross-model or language-model scale comparison, and no dense/MoE comparison or trillion-parameter models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No estimate of the share of interpretable neurons, no InceptionV1-sized model estimate, and no test of the claimed increase from about 5% to about 99%.
No attribution-graph reconstruction or comparison to a trained replacement model.
No test of explanations against activating examples versus held-out firing behavior.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: SpIn-ViT (Ours)
rows.operation_detail: Insertion evaluation using patches ranked by neuron activation; aggregate across datasets.
rows.note: The paper reports this as the highest insertion AUC among compared methods; the measure concerns attribution faithfulness, not neuron-job counts.
